**Finding submitted: `missing` (Rule TRANSITION), confidence 0.9**

**What I found.** Section 10 (Effect of Expiry or Termination) covers only three things: access cut-off after "any agreed transition period" (10.1), delivery of paid-for Deliverables, and refunds of prepaid Fees (10.2). Nothing in the Agreement obliges Vendor to return or export Customer Data, provide migration help, or delete data on a defined timeline:

- Searches for "transition", "export", and "delet" surface no substantive exit obligation — 10.1 merely *assumes* a transition period exists without creating a right to one.
- Section 15 (Customer Data and Privacy) imposes processing limits but no return duty.
- Section 16.5 requires return/destruction of Confidential Information but expressly carves Customer Data out to "Sections 11 and 15" — **and Section 11 does not exist in this document**, so the carve-out points nowhere. Customer Data currently falls through the gap entirely.

For a hosted-services agreement with a three-year term and a USD 2M/year take-or-pay commitment, this leaves us with no contractual exit path for our own data.

**Redline (validated, ok:true).** Inserted new Section 10.3 after p0042, tracking the playbook preferred position and the approved `seed-transition` precedent: (a) up to six months of transition assistance at Vendor's then-current rates, on request; (b) return/download of all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format within thirty days; (c) deletion thereafter with written certification. I added a "subject to routine backups and legal retention" qualifier to (c) for consistency with the existing Section 16.5 formulation — this keeps the clause consistent with the document's own drafting and avoids an easy Vendor objection.

**Direction check.** The clause binds Vendor only and imposes no new obligation on Juniper Ridge; the assistance is priced at Vendor's rates, so it is commercially proportionate. The comment flags the 90-day fallback in case Vendor resists the six-month tail.
